pr_title: Give each type of slider path type a unique colour to help visually distinguish them
pr_body:
The colours are just chosen to not clash. Not sure on whether they are "good" colours for each type, but seems to feel okay? Red is kept as linear because apparently that's what people are used to it representing in the majority of cases.

![20210319 140040 (dotnet)](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/191335/111733547-7f3e8e00-88bb-11eb-80e9-362378eebaf7.png)

Closes #12049.
pr_comments: Wouldn't a text label be better? Not sure colours improve things much.

Yeah, was planning on adding text. Possible as a tooltip? I think if we were to add it as an always-displayed label it will end up becoming clutter for some sliders (if you look at some of the sliders people create... there are a lot of nodes).

I was actually thinking of an always-displayed label. There are ways it could be done like displaying only on hover of any control points in the segment and/or for the closest segment to the mouse position when ctrl is held down, which could reduce clutter.

But let's go with this for now and see what people say.
Let me add a tooltip? Should work quite well.

I've chatted with some other mappers about this but I'd much prefer if you color coded the inherited nodes instead of the other (previously red) defining nodes like such: 
![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22646945/111724720-fb38c780-8822-11eb-9652-c89eec08a7fd.jpeg)

This gives much better visual understanding to how each slider section is behaving, especially since imo its the inherited nodes of the slider that really defines the slider shape for a particular part.

As a compromise (if you want to call it that), you could consider coloring each defining node a color, and then its inherited nodes a slightly different shade of that color while keeping the same base color?
@j-b-z I suggest making a new issue so that your post doesn't get lost.

issue_context.title: Slider sections' curve types don't get automatically upgraded like in osu-stable
issue_context.body: after you have created a slider that has at least one red node, adding new nodes doesnt make them white (curved) nodes, just red (angled) nodes (but they still look like white nodes) https://clips.twitch.tv/FitBlushingTruffleNotLikeThis-L4otvDzNukhiO9uu
comments:
Isn't this intended? Default curve type for newly created nodes is Inherit
[Example](https://puu.sh/HqrhA/ed27382992.mp4)

The difference here is that when the user places the first set of points, it's locking each segment into a linear type (because there are no nodes between the two red ones). In lazer, when adding a new node there, it's keeping the linear curve type, while in stable where there's no ability to select the curve per section, it's automatically upgrading it.

I'm not sure the best way of handling this. lazer's way makes more sense if you consider things from a fresh perspective, but it obviously doesn't match user expectations.

If the new node created between the red nodes is a linear type, then it should be red as well to properly reflect this nature. Right now, the new node is a yellow node and not a red one and so its pretty visually deceiving.

Ah I see. Is there anything that a linear section can achieve that just making new curve types with red nodes can't? Coming from stable it seems as if these linear type nodes are functionally behaving just like red nodes.

Edit: for clarity, it just feels like anything achievable with the linear type can just be done with a set of red nodes as well, so from my perspective as a stable mapper, I don't see why linear should exist and I'm pretty visually confused by them
I guess if you look at it that way, no? Except they are doing the same thing with far lower computational and clicking overhead.

Feels like mappers and modders lose some visual clarity by this (the stable preconceived notion is that red node -> sharp node and yellow/white node -> curve) but I guess it makes sense if the current red nodes are just more expensive to enable the multiple curve types
Might be able to improve things by showing the type of each red node inside or next to the control point circle.
Yeah actually color coding these different nodes types would be immensely useful for clarity

Can this turn into a feature request? I think it'd actually be so cool (and super good for visual clarity) to have inherited nodes be colored based off of what property its inheriting, since they do control the shape of that slider section.

Something like this:
![xYlOkN](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22646945/111724720-fb38c780-8822-11eb-9652-c89eec08a7fd.jpeg)
Yep, that will likely be the direction. I'll experiment with what works well.

review_comments: feels a bit too dark than other colours, what about: ```suggestion return colours.Purple; ``` before: after:

I was trying to make the lightness levels slightly different because I guarantee there's some colour-blindness mode where these two are indistinguishable (purple and pink seem quite close together).

The lighter one looks better but not sure.
Oh didn't take colour-blindness modes into account, yeah I think it's fine for now to keep distinguishing between each.

Perfect curve points get displayed as `PerfectCurve`, instead of a humanized form `Perfect curve`.
```csharp
        public string TooltipText => ControlPoint.Type.Value.ToString()?.Humanize() ?? string.Empty;
```
(need referencing/importing `Humanizer` namespace)
Was aware of this, but don't think it's that important. If anything it should be just `Perfect` or even something that is more understandable to the user like `Circular`.
